sections.heading: The teams are set
sections.text: Gemma’s teams turn back to their workbenches. Entry and team mergers closed Wednesday. Now each test has to earn its place. Kaggle caps uploads at one a day. The final submission deadline is 2 December 2026, 23:59 UTC.

sections.heading: Pick what goes in the case
sections.text:
Teams can pick up to two submissions for final judging. If a team makes no choice, Kaggle handles the selection. Each agent writes patches for software issues. Its score is the share of patched repositories that pass the validation tests. The private board uses a separate test set to rank the entries and determine the potential winners.

That makes the last upload and the final selection two different calls. If one build shines on the public board, does a team send another version of it or give a different approach a seat?

review.notes: Verified the official Kaggle timeline, limits, defaults, scoring and private-board language. Independent Claude reviews led to a clearer deadline, automatic selection without an assumed count, the patched-repository denominator, the potential-winner wording and an explicitly hypothetical closing question. The final reviewer recommended publication and asked for an illustration label. The caption identifies the scene as imagined by The Loose Goose. Earlier flags about proof metadata referred to the review wrapper. The filed dispatch contains no competitor, rank or cast row. The fresh built-in ImageGen scene uses the David Sarrat Gemma portrait only for set style. Visual inspection at full size and 390 pixels confirmed both case slots, the anonymous glove and rocket. The decorations carry no numbers or text. No regalia or nameplate appears. This review binds the exact caption, dispatch and WebP.
